title: Nonnegativity of Bob's special-coordinate information term
statement:
Fix a positive integer $n$ and a deterministic communication protocol $p$ for the disjointness problem on inputs indexed by $\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$. Draw a sample from the hard distribution over inputs, conditioned on the event that Alice's set and Bob's set are disjoint, and consider the following random variables: the special coordinate $T$; Alice's input bits $X_{\le T}$ at coordinates up to and including $T$ (padded by $0$ elsewhere); Bob's input bits $Y_{>T}$ at coordinates strictly above $T$ (padded by $0$ elsewhere); Bob's bit $Y_T$ at the special coordinate; and the transcript $M$ obtained by running $p$ on the generated input pair. Then the conditional mutual information of $Y_T$ and $M$ given the tuple $(T, X_{\le T}, Y_{>T})$ is nonnegative:
\[
I\bigl(Y_T : M \mid T, X_{\le T}, Y_{>T}\bigr) \ge 0.
\]
hypotheses_covered: p is a deterministic disjointness protocol
the hard distribution conditioned on the disjointness event
the quantity is the conditional mutual information I(Y_T : M | T, X_{≤T}, Y_{>T})
replaced: Bob's corrected information term is nonnegative.
